stem: Meera finds an unlabelled bottle of a colourless liquid in her kitchen. She knows that sour-tasting foods like lemon (citric acid) and curd (lactic acid) contain acids. Which is the correct and safe way to think about the unknown liquid?

options.text: Taste a drop of it; if it is sour, it must be an acid
It may be acidic, but unknown substances must never be tasted; test it safely with blue litmus paper instead
It is safe to drink because sour taste means it is a food acid
It is acidic only if it is yellow like lemon juice

teacher.key_rationale: Tasting unknown substances is unsafe; sour taste links common foods to named acids, but identification of an unknown liquid must use a safe test such as litmus. B is the only option that both connects sour taste with food acids and preserves the safety rule.
